subject: general
question: What is the SI unit of 'volume'?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cubic metre.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cubic metre__ is the SI unit of volume.
 
• It is denoted by m³.
 
• One cubic metre is equivalent to 1000 litres.
 
• It is used to measure the volume of substances or objects in three-dimensional space.
 
• Commonly used in scientific, industrial, and everyday applications.
 
• Examples include the measurement of liquids, gases, or solids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Litre:**

 
 
• A litre is a non-SI unit of volume equivalent to 1/1000 of a cubic metre (0.001 m³).
 
• It is commonly used for measuring liquids and fluids in everyday life.
 
 
 
• **Millilitre:**
 
 
• It is a metric unit of volume, equal to one-thousandth of a litre (0.001 L).
 
• Often used in pharmaceuticals and cooking measurements.
 
 
 
• **Cubic Centimetre:**
 
 
• A cubic centimetre (cm³) is a metric unit of volume.
 
• It is equivalent to a millilitre (1 cm³ = 1 mL).
